title: Bay Area's 'Little Fire' Forces Thousands to Evacuate as Blaze Tops 1,000 Acres Near Pleasanton
excerpt: A fast-moving wildfire south of Pleasanton in Alameda County has injured at least one firefighter and triggered evacuation orders across six zones, including the Ruby Hill neighborhood.
body:
• The Little Fire erupted south of Pleasanton on Tuesday afternoon and rapidly grew to over 1,000 acres with only 10% containment.
  • Evacuation orders cover six zones including the Ruby Hill neighborhood, affecting thousands of residents in Alameda County.
  • At least one firefighter has been injured; CAL FIRE says crews face limited access and extreme heat.
  • Multiple agencies including CAL FIRE, Alameda County Fire Department, and Livermore-Pleasanton Fire Department are battling the blaze from ground and air.

Wildfire Explodes Across Alameda County Hills

A fast-moving wildfire dubbed the Little Fire broke out south of Pleasanton in Alameda County on Tuesday afternoon and rapidly grew to more than 1,000 acres, forcing evacuation orders for thousands of residents across the East Bay.

The fire ignited sometime before 3 p.m. near Little Valley Road and Hubbard Lane in the Sunol area, according to CAL FIRE. Fueled by dry vegetation and high temperatures, the blaze tore through grassy hillsides at a rapid rate of spread, sending heavy smoke billowing across the Tri-Valley region visible from miles away.

As of Tuesday evening, the fire had reached approximately 1,007 acres with only 10% containment, according to CAL FIRE data. At least one firefighter sustained injuries during the response, though details about the severity were not immediately released.

Thousands Under Evacuation Orders

Authorities issued evacuation orders for six zones: ALC-072, PLS-079, PLS-080, PLS-081, PLS-082, and PLS-103. The orders cover the Ruby Hill neighborhood, an affluent gated community in southern Pleasanton, as well as other residential areas near the fire's path.

The blaze was burning dangerously close to several homes along Little Valley Road, according to KRON4. Residents in the affected zones were directed to leave immediately, and evacuation centers were being set up in the surrounding area.

"Firefighters are being challenged by limited access and hot weather."

— CAL FIRE

The New York Times reported that the fire prompted evacuation orders affecting thousands of residents, making it one of the most disruptive wildfires in the Bay Area this summer.

Multi-Agency Response from Ground and Air

The firefighting response drew resources from multiple agencies. Crews from the Alameda County Fire Department and Livermore-Pleasanton Fire Department joined CAL FIRE personnel in battling the blaze from both ground and air. Helicopters and air tankers made repeated drops on the fire's advancing front, while ground crews worked to establish containment lines in the steep, brush-covered terrain.

CAL FIRE noted that limited road access in the rugged hills south of Pleasanton was complicating the response. The area between Pleasanton and Sunol is characterized by narrow rural roads and steep terrain that makes deploying heavy equipment difficult.

California's Relentless Fire Season

The Little Fire is the latest in a punishing 2026 wildfire season across California. The state is simultaneously fighting the Biscar Fire in Lassen and Washoe counties, which has burned over 69,000 acres, along with the Rock Fire in Inyo County and the Elephant Fire in the northern Sierra Nevada. Combined, active California wildfires have scorched well over 100,000 acres this month alone.

"Crews from the Alameda County Fire Department and Livermore-Pleasanton Fire Department joined CAL FIRE personnel in battling the blaze from both ground and air."

The Tri-Valley corridor — encompassing Pleasanton, Dublin, and Livermore — is home to a large and growing population, including a significant Indian American community. The Ruby Hill neighborhood alone contains hundreds of upscale homes, and the evacuation orders have displaced families across a wide swath of southern Pleasanton.

What to Watch

With containment at just 10%, firefighters face a critical window over the coming hours. High temperatures and dry conditions are forecast to persist across the East Bay through midweek, potentially fueling further fire growth. Residents in surrounding zones should monitor the Alameda County emergency alert system and CAL FIRE incident updates for any changes to evacuation orders or warnings.

The cause of the Little Fire remains under investigation.
